description: Requirements for VAST (Video Ad Serving Template) creative assets.

media_file_requirements.description: Technical acceptance constraints for the alternative MediaFile renditions in each applicable resolved InLine linear creative.

codecs.description: Accepted codec identifiers for `MediaFile@codec`, using the codec syntax referenced by the applicable VAST version. A missing codec attribute does not satisfy a declared codec constraint unless safe inspection establishes the codec.

containers.description: Accepted normalized container identifiers, such as `mp4`, `webm`, or `mpeg_ts`. A receiver MUST determine the container from authoritative metadata or safe byte inspection and MUST NOT guess it only from the media URI suffix.

delivery_methods.description: Accepted values of the required `MediaFile@delivery` attribute. `progressive` identifies a directly downloadable media file; `streaming` identifies a streaming media resource.

items.description: Delivery method declared by the required VAST MediaFile `delivery` attribute.
items.title: VAST Media Delivery Method

max_bitrate_kbps.description: Maximum accepted MediaFile bitrate in kilobits per second. A fixed `MediaFile@bitrate` must not exceed this value. For adaptive/streaming media, the declared `MediaFile@maxBitrate` must not exceed this value. Safe byte inspection may establish the value when metadata is absent.

max_file_size_bytes.description: Maximum accepted MediaFile size in exact bytes. `MediaFile@fileSize`, when present, is expressed in bytes; a receiver MAY verify it against safely fetched media bytes and MUST use the verified byte count if the values disagree.

mime_types.description: Accepted MIME types from `MediaFile@type`, compared case-insensitively after trimming optional whitespace. Parameters are not accepted in this field. Examples: `video/mp4`, `video/webm`, `audio/mpeg`, `audio/aac`.

min_bitrate_kbps.description: Minimum accepted MediaFile bitrate in kilobits per second. A fixed `MediaFile@bitrate` must be at least this value. For adaptive/streaming media, the declared `MediaFile@minBitrate` must be at least this value. Safe byte inspection may establish the value when metadata is absent.

media_file_requirements.title: VAST MediaFile Requirements

verifier_constraints.adaptive_bitrate_containment: A MediaFile advertising a minBitrate/maxBitrate interval satisfies declared bitrate bounds only when its entire interval is contained within those bounds; overlap alone is insufficient.
verifier_constraints.alternative_renditions: For each applicable resolved InLine linear creative, at least one MediaFile MUST satisfy every declared property in this object; requirements MUST NOT be satisfied by combining properties from different MediaFile elements.
verifier_constraints.missing_metadata: If a declared property cannot be established from VAST metadata or safe inspection, compatibility is unproven and the MediaFile does not satisfy that property.
verifier_constraints.range_order: When both bounds are declared, min_width MUST be <= max_width, min_height MUST be <= max_height, and min_bitrate_kbps MUST be <= max_bitrate_kbps.

vast_version.$comment: VAST 4.3 ships no XSD of its own: IAB's `vast_4.2.xsd` remains the authoritative schema for 4.3 documents, so a validator MUST NOT reject a tag declaring `version="4.3"` for want of a 4.3 schema. VAST 4.4 is deliberately absent because `vast_4.4.xsd` is annotated 'DRAFT for working group discussion' and is not a published specification; add it once IAB publishes it, not before. This file is the single source of truth for the roster, per the Enum Consolidation rule in docs/spec-guidelines.md, and other schemas `$ref` it rather than restating the list.
vast_version.description: Deprecated one-element alias for `vast_versions`. Producers use either the singular legacy alias or the plural 3.2 field, never both.
vast_version.title: VAST Version

vast_versions.description: Accepted VAST version set for this asset requirement.
